chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan from Sind ibn Muhammad from 'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: I heard him say:

Al-Fay' and Al-Anfal: whatever is from land where there was no shedding of blood and people were reconciled and gave with their own hands, and whatever is from barren land or the bottoms of valleys, then it is all from Al-Fay'. So this is for Allah and His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family); and whatever is for Allah is for His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), who places it where he wills, and it is for the Imam (peace be upon him) after the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family).
And His saying: 'And what Allah has bestowed upon His Messenger from them, so you did not mount for it [a campaign of] cavalry or camels.'

He said: 'Do you not see? It is this.' And as for His saying: 'What Allah has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns,' this is in the status of Al-Maghanim (booty). My father (peace be upon him) used to say: 'That is it, and we have in it no more than two shares: the share of the Messenger and the share of the Close Relatives, then we are partners with the people in what remains.'

key_terms.الْأَنْفَالُ: Al-Anfal (plunder/booty, often used broadly for divine gains)
key_terms.الْفَيْءُ: Al-Fay' (booty/gains from which no fighting occurred)
key_terms.الْفَيْءُ وَالْأَنْفَالُ: The concept of Fay' and Anfal combined
key_terms.سَهْمِ الْقُرْبَى: Share of the Close Relatives (Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Al-Fay' and Al-Anfal in Shia jurisprudence and who receives the shares?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates Al-Fay' as property acquired without military exertion, such as barren lands or reconciled tribes, which belongs exclusively to Allah and the Prophet, and subsequently to the Imam as his successor. In contrast, booty from towns (Al-Maghanim) follows the standard distribution model where the Ahl al-Bayt receive two shares before sharing the remainder with the people, highlighting the unique fiscal authority of the Imams in Shia jurisprudence.
